title: Predicted High-Energy Molecules: Helical All-Nitrogen and Helical Nitrogen-Rich Ring Clusters
notes_general: N26H16 ([6] N-helicene, Figure 3) is OUT OF SCOPE (contains H). Both in-scope species (N26, N46) are large NEW helical all-nitrogen cage/ring-fusion structures, both confirmed as genuine energy minima by the authors' own frequency analysis (all real eigenvalues) -- larger than anything in the existing 70-structure corpus (max N20) or the N_csp/polyN_study imports (max N12), so very likely genuinely new to the full pool.

species.point_group: not stated (nonplanar, described as C1-like helical, no symmetry label given)

bond_params.shape: helical fused chain of 6 six-membered N rings ('[6] N-ring helix'), boat-conformation rings at both ends, nonplanar overall structure

species.notes: Confirmed true minimum (real frequencies for all Hessian eigenvectors). Energy 864.6 kcal/mol above 13 N2. Dissociation to 2N2 releases 210.6 kcal/mol but barrier is only 4.85 kJ/mol (~1.16 kcal/mol) -- essentially barrierless, authors state this is 'insufficient to keep [6] N-ring helix kinetically stable' despite being a true PES minimum. Important caveat for any future metastability/HEDM discussion of this structure.

bond_params.shape: helical fused chain of 11 six-membered N rings ('[11] N-ring helix'), boat conformation at end rings
bond_params.confidence: good -- explicitly labeled a/b/c/d/e lettered bonds with small ring diagrams in Figure 2, ranges given rather than single point values (repeating helical unit varies slightly along the helix)

species.notes: Confirmed true minimum (real frequencies). Energy 1538.0 kcal/mol above 23 N2. Bonds b,c in end units close to N=N double bond length; most other bonds close to N-N single bond; one bond (d, intermediate units) elongated up to 1.597 A on some ring positions -- notably long/weak N-N bond, possible point of instability.
